newsitem.title: CANADA: ALPINE SKIING-SLALOM CHAMP WIBERG WINS WOMEN'S WORLD CUP SUPER-G.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SLALOM CHAMP WIBERG WINS WOMEN'S WORLD CUP SUPER-G.

text.p: World slalom
champion Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden won the first women's World
Cup super-G of the season Sunday, again showing her improving
skills in the speed events along with her slalom prowess.
One day after finishing third in the downhill, Wiberg
collected the 14th victory of her World Cup career in 1
minute, 22.12 seconds. Former world junior super-G champion
Hilde Gerg of Germany was second in 1:22.43 over the 1.9 km
course in Lake Louise.
"I shared a super-G win in Cortina in '94 with (Slovenian
Alenka) Dovzan so now I have one all by myself," the
wide-smiling Wiberg said at the finish.
Warwara Zelenskaja of Russia posted her best super-G
result, third place in 1:22.75. Frenchwoman Florence Masnada
was fourth in 1:23.00 and defending World Cup overall champion
Katja Seizinger of Germany fifth with a 1:23.04 clocking.
German skiers filled five of the top 10 spots. Martina
Ertl -- racing after suffering a ligament injury in her left
knee on October 14 -- was eighth, Miriam Vogt ninth and
Katharina Gutensohn 10th.
After five races, Seizinger, the downhill winner Saturday,
leads the World Cup points tally with 305. Wiberg is second at
258. Gerg stands third with 208.
Wiberg was the fastest down the first third of the race,
which gave her a lead no one else could overcome.
"The top of the course was set like a giant slalom and the
bottom was like a downhill, so it had the turns, and the speed
at the bottom," she said. "And since I like both types of
skiing, I didn't have much problem."
Although she has shown dramatically improved downhill and
super-G results, Wiberg said she isn't thinking about the
overall title.
"I thought of that before and I think I put too much
pressure on myself. This year, my goal was to ski well in
slalom and maybe win a downhill," said Wiberg, who won the
gold medal in slalom and combined at the 1996 world
championships in Spain last February.
Gerg, starting sixth, had the fastest time on the bottom
of the course as she recorded her best World Cup super-G
result since winning at Sierra Nevada in a pre-Olympic
downhill in 1994.
"The snow from overnight was no problem. It wasn't soft or
rutted when I skied. The slope was OK for me," Gerg said.
Zelenskaja, best known as a downhiller, clapped her hands
joyously as she skied through the finish area after her strong
race. "This is so great," she said, "so very great."
